_comment: Accepted-risk allowlist for scripts/check-audit.js.
CI fails on any advisory NOT listed here, so adding an entry is a deliberate,
reviewable act — not a silent suppression. Each entry must say why the
advisory cannot bite THIS codebase, verified against actual usage rather than
the advisory text, and what would make it bite (the tripwire).
`reviewBy` does not fail the build; it prints a loud warning once passed, so
an acceptance cannot quietly become permanent. Established by the 2026-07-29
review — see docs/reviews/technical-review-2026-07-29.md §3 finding 4.
2026-08-09 review pass (exploratory-program close-out /audit): 12 advisories
had accumulated unreviewed since the last pass and the gate had been red on
master for some time. Each was verified against real usage — imports checked,
not advisory text read — and none is exploitable here. The stale react-router
entry (GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2) was removed: the advisory no longer matches, so
keeping it would have made the list lie about what it is protecting.
2026-09-24 pass (blanket `npm audit fix`, shipped with the self-host fix): the
10 advisories published since the last pass all had non-breaking fixes, so
they were upgraded rather than allowlisted. The same upgrade fixed 11 entries
below (dompurify, hono x4, js-yaml, undici x5); they were removed for the same
reason as the react-router entry above.
2026-09-30 pass (`npm audit fix --package-lock-only`, shipped with the
Cloudflare-review fixes): 13 advisories published since the last pass
(brace-expansion x3, undici x10, all in build/dev tooling) had non-breaking
fixes, so they were upgraded rather than allowlisted: wrangler 4.138 -> 4.145
(miniflare + workerd with it) and brace-expansion 1.1.15 -> 1.1.21. The same
upgrade fixed the three brace-expansion entries below; they were removed.
2026-10-03 (view-rotation PR #95): GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (braces, high) was
published after master's last green run. Every braces version is affected and
npm's only remedy is a breaking tsc-alias downgrade, so it is allowlisted below
(dev-only, verified against the lockfile) rather than upgraded.
`scope` names the tree an entry was reviewed against: "root" (the workspace
lockfile) or "backend" (packages/axoview-backend/package-lock.json, prod deps
only: the tree the Docker image installs). Use ["root", "backend"] when the
advisory is in both. An entry without `scope` covers "root" only, so a
dev-only acceptance can never silently cover a package the image ships.
2026-11-04 (AI manual PR #40): GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (minimatch, moderate) was
published that day. Its range is every release below 11.0.1 and every locked
copy comes from dev tooling (eslint, jest, typescript-eslint, madge, nodemon,
semantic-release's npm), so it is allowlisted below rather than forced to 11.

allow.title: Quill XSS via HTML export feature
allow.why: Axoview DOES call the affected getSemanticHTML(), but every call site pipes the result through sanitizeHtml() before it is stored (TextBoxInlineEditor.tsx:132,151), the model is re-sanitized on load (useInitialDataManager.ts:90), and the sole dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink re-sanitizes at render (TextBox.tsx:343). ADR 0029's defence-in-depth absorbs the payload. Re-reviewed 2026-10-29: all three sanitize points still in place, still no forward fix.
allow.noForwardFix: npm's only remedy is a BREAKING downgrade to react-quill-new@3.7.0.
allow.tripwire: If the ADR 0029 sanitize is removed from ANY of those three points, this becomes live stored-XSS. renderedGeometry-style contract coverage on sanitizeHtml call sites would make that unmissable.

allow.title: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
allow.why: The only locked instance is deepmerge@4.3.1 under jest -> @jest/core -> jest-config, marked dev in the lock; `npm ls deepmerge --omit=dev` is empty and it is absent from packages/axoview-backend/package-lock.json. jest-config uses it to merge this repo's own jest config files, so every merged object is authored here and no attacker-controlled input reaches mergeObject(). It is in neither browser bundle nor the Docker image.
allow.noForwardFix: The range is >=4.2.0: no deepmerge release fixes it, and npm's only remedy is a breaking downgrade of jest to 25.1.0.
allow.tripwire: Re-review immediately if deepmerge enters a production tree or any runtime code merges user-supplied objects with it. Drop this entry once a patched deepmerge ships or jest stops depending on it.

allow.title: minimatch has potential denial of service via globparts amplification
allow.why: Every locked minimatch (3.1.5, 10.2.4-10.2.6) is marked dev in the root lockfile, under eslint/@eslint/*, jest's glob and test-exclude, @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree, madge's detective-typescript, nodemon and semantic-release's bundled npm; `npm ls minimatch --omit=dev` is empty and the backend's production tree (check-audit [backend]) has no advisory. No Axoview source file or script imports minimatch. The amplification needs an attacker-chosen glob pattern; these tools only expand patterns written in this repo's own configs (eslint.config.mjs, jest configs, madge/knip settings), so no outside input reaches it. It is in neither browser bundle nor the Docker image.
allow.noForwardFix: The fix is minimatch 11.0.1, a major release none of these tools accepts yet; npm's only offered remedy is a breaking semantic-release downgrade to 20.1.3.
allow.tripwire: Re-review immediately if minimatch enters a production tree, or any runtime code or CI step expands a glob taken from user or PR-author input (for example a workflow that globs a path from an issue or PR body). Drop this entry once eslint, jest and the others move to minimatch >= 11.0.1.
